help_quickstart_scan_desc: Go to the Games page and click "Scan All" to detect installed games from Steam and Epic Games. You can also add games manually by pointing to their executable.
help_quickstart_monitor_desc: Click "Start" in the monitoring widget in the sidebar. GameRoute will automatically detect when a monitored game is running and capture network connections.
help_quickstart_sessions_desc: A session is created each time a monitored game is detected. It records server IPs, traceroutes, and network quality data until the game closes.
help_glossary_asn_desc: A unique identifier for a group of IP networks managed by one or more operators. Helps identify which network provider owns an IP address.
help_glossary_ttl_desc: A counter that limits the lifespan of a network packet. Each router decrements the TTL by one. Traceroute uses this to discover each hop along the route.
help_glossary_traceroute_desc: A network diagnostic tool that maps the path packets take from your computer to a server. It reveals each router (hop) along the way and measures latency at each step.
help_glossary_problem_hop_desc: A router along the traceroute path that shows significantly higher latency (>50ms increase) or packet loss (>10%). This may indicate a network bottleneck.
help_glossary_ip_period_desc: A continuous time window during which your game communicated with a specific server IP. Multiple periods can exist for the same IP within one session.
help_glossary_packet_loss_desc: The percentage of network packets that fail to reach their destination. High packet loss causes lag, rubber-banding, and disconnections in games.
help_faq_no_geo: Why do some IPs have no geolocation?
help_faq_no_geo_answer: Geolocation data comes from third-party databases that may not cover all IPs. Private or recently allocated IPs often lack location information.
help_faq_manual_game: How do I add a game manually?
help_faq_manual_game_answer: Go to the Games page, click "Add Game", enter the game name and browse to select the game's executable file (.exe on Windows, .app on macOS).
help_faq_high_latency_answer: High latency can be caused by geographic distance to the server, network congestion, ISP routing issues, or problems at specific hops along the route. Check the Network and Insights pages to identify patterns.
help_faq_no_data_collection_answer: No. GameRoute does not collect any personal data. All your session data, game library, and network analysis are stored locally on your machine in a SQLite database and are never transmitted to any server. The only external communication is with ip-api.com to resolve IP geolocation (see the Data & APIs section below).
help_data_description: GameRoute uses the following external services to enrich network analysis. No personal data is sent — only IP addresses encountered during traceroutes.
help_data_ip_api_desc: Used to resolve geolocation (country, city, coordinates), ASN, and ISP for IP addresses encountered during traceroutes. Requests are batched and rate-limited. Data is cached locally for 30 days.
